title: Cascade: Efficient Multi-GPU Synchronization for DNN Training
problem: Synchronization overhead during gradient aggregation in distributed DNN training limits throughput and scalability across multiple GPUs.
motivation: Reducing synchronization overhead is critical for efficient large-scale DNN training, enabling faster convergence and better resource utilization.
method: Cascade uses hierarchical reduction trees to organize multi-GPU synchronization into layers, reducing total communication overhead. It employs adaptive batch sizing to dynamically balance computation and synchronization costs based on system characteristics. The approach optimizes collective reduction operations during gradient synchronization in data-parallel distributed training.
key_novelty: Combining hierarchical reduction trees with adaptive batch sizing to dynamically optimize the synchronization-computation tradeoff in distributed DNN training.
contributions: Hierarchical reduction tree approach for organizing multi-GPU synchronization
Adaptive batch sizing strategy responsive to system characteristics
40% throughput improvement in distributed DNN training on large-scale models
primary_theme: Multi-GPU synchronization optimization for distributed DNN training
